notes.title: Thank you (Dev #4)
notes.content:
[h1]Release[/h1]
So, the game released nearly a week ago. First of all, thank you to everyone that has played it! 
The release went more or less how we expected and we're quite happy with it.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39465681/b190e3b7fc59e0de150531dda05db123a2690069.png[/img]

Very soon after came in some bugs related to achievements which we promptly fixed, and after that, a major bug as Windows 7 users could not get past the main menu. This is our fault as we don't actually have access to a Windows 7 machine and just assumed it worked because of Unity. 

[h1]Leading up to release[/h1]
There was a bit of a rough time as we were constantly working up to the release hour. Just a day before release we found out a major bug that was making the game unplayable and we even considered doing a last minute delay. In the end it wasn't needed as we managed to fix that bug and some others :)
The music and extra sound effects were added on the release day, that's how close we were.

[h1]About that achievement...[/h1]
One of our achievements [spoiler]Bullet Train[/spoiler].. We admit we didn't actually test it to know if it was possible to earn it. As it turns out, either it was REALLY hard or literally impossible to earn it. We looked around what to do as changing an achievement requirement after launch doesn't seem so good. Thing is we weren't even sure if anyone had managed to unlock it legitimately, so we ended up changing the requirement before too long. And since then we can confirm that it is indeed possible :)

[h1]What's on the horizon?[/h1]
We took a bit of a break after the release regarding working on new features. We've been discussing on what to add, and here's some of our ideas.

[h3]Difficulty levels[/h3]
Allow you to choose between Easy, Normal or Hard.

[h3]Speedrunning Mode[/h3]
This one is mostly for our amusement as we jokingly say we'd like to see a speedrun of Loopomotive, and one way to make that more likely to happen is to add a speedrunning mode. 

[h3]Controller support[/h3]
This one was actually planned for release but we didn't manage to do it as our programmer doesn't actually have a controller so that he can test with ːlunar2019piginablanketː So, we're looking to fix that.

[h3]Others[/h3]
If you have any wishes or ideas, do let us know so we can at least consider them.

notes.title: Preparing for release (Dev #3)
notes.content:
Hello!

We've been working whenever we can on Loopomotive since the last development blog and you might have noticed that we've marked the game for release. The game will be released on March 31 2021!

[h1]Preparing for the release[/h1]
March 31 had been the target date since we had decided to make the game for Steam. We were comfortable that this gave us enough time and we haven't felt much pressure although there is still some features and bugs that we'd like to add and iron out before release, but the game is perfectly playable :)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39465681/ede5a33e00cd12332691b89f874f3c9f0d63db3d.png[/img]
[i]How the game was made[/i]

[h1]Current work[/h1]
There's still one feature we'd like to add before it releases and that is train Skins. There's also strange a bug where cars sometimes disappear (very rarely) which we're looking at.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39465681/f7a522a60ed5a361e05d9fa5f22476f5851302be.png[/img]
[i]With skins, you can customise your train[/i]

[h1]Why is the game free[/h1]
You might be thinking it's a 'free to play' game, but actually no, it's a FREE game. We're not making any money out of it. 
We've been making small games together for years now and we wanted to make a push towards a more 'professional' game, something we can point at and be proud of, and this will be the result. We have learned a lot about Game Development in the process and finding out all the little details that you never think about or take for granted when playing games.
There isn't that much content but enough to keep you entertained for a couple hours and we've polished what's there and for all intents and purposes we're treating it as a 'paid' game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39465681/a4a27da3ad4217ff926b12131ba32d62befac70c.png[/img]
[i]How the graphics were made[/i]

[h1]After release[/h1]
We're not expecting a big fanfare release, especially when we haven't really marketed the game, but instead a very small release. We're not even sure if people will like the game but it's ok, we managed to do it and that's what counts for us :) Of course we'll be listening to feedback and fixing any bugs that people find. 
As for future content updates? We don't know yet. We don't want to promise anything but we have a small list of wishes and ideas that might be added at some point.

[b]This probably will be the last Dev Blog before release so, we'll see you on the other side and we hope you like the game![/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39465681/b190e3b7fc59e0de150531dda05db123a2690069.png[/img]

notes.title: Polishing (Dev #2)
notes.content:
Hello, welcome to our Development Blog #2!

The game has progressed a fair bit and we've now entered the polishing and wrapping up stage. This means that we've finished most of the main content and now we have to tie up systems like Main Menu, Save & Load, Settings, and so on. Also take the time to improve graphics and other tiny things everywhere.

[h1]Progress[/h1]
[h2]Levels are done! ːwinter2019happyyulː[/h2]
We have created and finished all the levels that we want to release with. 15 levels, all with unique art and different track or premise.
However, there's still a lot that can be done on these levels. Tiny touches and polishing to make the experience better.

We have also locked in the overworld progression for the levels, and in the progress we even got some ideas for possible future levels.

[h2]Main Menu[/h2]
We've started working on the new main menu. Up to this point we've had the same one from Ludum Dare version. Here's a sneak peak of how it looks now:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39465681/8a88e21135c7e48847a71307d90905ac445fa3ac.png[/img]

It is fully animated but we'll save that to when the game releases :)

[h1]Resolutions & Aspect Ratios[/h1]
If you're keen on aspect ratios, you'll notice that the main menu screenshot is 21:9. So I think this is a great time to talk about our journey with dealing on scaling the game to fit into different screens.

Our Ludum Dare version was locked and designed at 960x600, which is 16:10. It was meant to be played on the browser without the need to go full-screen. While this is great for a web game, it doesn't quite fit when you go into Steam. On a Steam game people expect a full-screen game at any resolution.

We started tinkering with what kind of resolutions we wanted to support. Knowingly that many people will for the most part have a 16:9 or 16:10 screen we could have just scaled up. But in order to future proof the game a little bit, we decided to support wider screens as more and more people have them. [b]So the game will support up to 21:9 wide-screen resolutions[/b]. Initially we even considered about 32:9 but the amount of effort vs 'wasted art' that only a handful would see didn't seem worth it.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39465681/dd3298c87c0cf470f36a6270dbaffb0612bf5ac0.png[/img]

The playable game area still has to fit within 16:9, and that also happens to be the maximum aspect ratio at which our computer screens can reach anyway :) All this said, the game should also be playable at lower resolutions since we still once in a while take a peek of how it would look at our original 960x600 resolution.

tags.feature: So the game will support up to 21:9 wide-screen resolutions

notes.title: Hello, Loopomotive (Dev #1)
notes.content:
Hello everyone!

This is our first development blog, ever, so bear with us :)

[h1]Who we are[/h1]
We're Shy Pixel, our adopted group name. We're 2 people, we're shy and we've always had some passion for everything game related.

One of us is specialized in Programming and the other in Art. So there's a lot of stuff in the middle that we have to branch out and figure out ourselves.

We've been working on Loopomotive ever since the game came out from Ludum Dare. The progress hasn't been up to what we probably wish, as we both have to deal with full-time jobs on the side, but we're quite proud and eager to share of what we've done so far.

This isn't the first time we're working on a game together, but it is the first in what we consider to be more than a "demo". Loopomotive will be free as we're not looking into making money from it.

[h1]Progress[/h1]
[h2]Levels, levels and more levels[/h2]
Our Ludum Dare entry had only 3 levels, and we've been aiming to expand at least 5x that. Each level is unique in the art and sometimes even contain special features. Here's some of them: [b]Graveyard[/b], [b]Sky[/b], [b]Space[/b], [b]Lava[/b], [b]Mushroom Forest[/b].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39465681/0d3e6d05134a9677911891a9cee451c3cbd61ee6.png[/img]

[h2]Goal[/h2]
We've added different goal types, and now a level can be beat based on time or number of loops. The good ol' number of cars is still present.

[h2]Abilities[/h2]
Emergency brake. There's been too many times when you know you're about to crash into a car, but now you can use the emergency brake as a last resort measure. It takes time to recharge so it won't be there to save you every single time.

[h1]Current State[/h1]
We're getting close to the release. Once we finish up how much content we want to put in, it's time to start polishing away and making things better. We still have to re-do the main menu and implement a settings menu. Then we might still have time to add some nice to have features, as we'd like to implement Steam Achievements at least.

We're hoping to make the development a more common occurrence as we think transparency and sharing is quite good for game development and the fans.

Thank you for following along with us!
